arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import numpy as np

# USDA outlays data from Treasury Bulletins (in millions of dollars)
# Years 1990-1998, with 1990 as year 0
years = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]  # 1990-1998
outlays = [46011, 54119, 56436, 63143, 60812, 56667, 54338, 52558, 53949]

# Perform linear regression
x = np.array(years)
y = np.array(outlays)

n = len(years)
sum_x = np.sum(x)
sum_y = np.sum(y)
sum_xy = np.sum(x * y)
sum_x2 = np.sum(x**2)

# Calculate slope (m) and y-intercept (b)
slope = (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x**2)
y_intercept = (sum_y - slope * sum_x) / n

# Predicted value for 1999 (year 9)
year_1999 = 9
predicted = slope * year_1999 + y_intercept

print(f"Data points (year, outlay):")
for i, (yr, out) in enumerate(zip(years, outlays)):
    print(f"  {yr} (1990+{yr}): {out}")

print(f"\nLinear Regression Results:")
print(f"  Slope: {slope}")
print(f"  Y-intercept: {y_intercept}")
print(f"  Predicted for 1999 (year 9): {predicted}")

print(f"\nRounded values:")
print(f"  Slope (rounded to nearest hundredth): {round(slope, 2)}")
print(f"  Y-intercept (rounded to nearest whole number): {round(y_intercept)}")
print(f"  Predicted value (rounded to nearest whole number): {round(predicted)}")

print(f"\nFinal answer format: [slope, y-intercept, predicted]")
print(f"  [{round(slope, 2)}, {round(y_intercept)}, {round(predicted)}]")
EOF
